extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists and newsroom staff (and journalists/readers seeking Reuters' editorial standards)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Reuters journalists on ethical principles and everyday newsroom behaviour — emphasising independence, accuracy, integrity and professional judgement rather than rigid rules. Intended to map principles for decision-making in reporting across text, TV and pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Everything we do as Reuters journalists has to be independent..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook states that Reuters journalism must be independent; independence is cited as a core value stemming from the Reuters Trust Principles and underpins all reporting decisions. Independence is paired with other core values (see integrity, freedom from bias).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting must be free from bias; impartiality in coverage is an explicit core value and expectation for Reuters journalists. This implies avoiding slanted language, selective sourcing, or partisan presentation of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: "...executed with the utmost integrity. These are our core values and stem from the Reuters Trust Principles."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are expected to act with integrity in all aspects of their work. Integrity is a foundational value that governs behaviour and is linked to adherence to the Reuters Trust Principles and Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters values accuracy as a primary newsroom value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy is essential to Reuters' reputation as a real-time, competitive news service. Journalists must prioritise factual correctness in reporting and verification processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters values speed in its news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speed is an operational value for a real-time news service, but it is presented alongside accuracy and exclusivity — implying speed should not compromise accuracy or integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters values exclusivity as part of its service offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusivity (obtaining unique content or scoops) is valued, but must be pursued within the framework of ethical practice and other core values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the Reuters Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: "The way in which we, as Reuters employees, live these values is governed by the Reuters Code of Conduct."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are expected to follow the Code of Conduct; while the Handbook notes some notable exceptions apply specifically to journalists, the Code governs behaviour of all Reuters employees and is 'essential reading.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek and report the truth fairly, honestly and unfailingly
rubrics_metrics.description: "As journalists, however, we have additional responsibilities if we are to fulfil the highest aspirations of our profession - to search for and report the truth, fairly, honestly and unfailingly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic responsibility is framed as an active duty to pursue truth and report it without distortion, dishonesty, or omission. This criterion encapsulates fairness, honesty, and relentless commitment to factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: "Beyond the obvious, such as the cardinal sin of plagiarism..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism is identified as a cardinal sin and unacceptable. Journalists must not present others' work as their own and should attribute and cite appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fabrication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making up facts, sources, quotations or events is explicitly condemned. Fabrication is labelled dishonest and a core violation of journalistic ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bribe-taking (improper payments)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting bribes or improper payments is immoral and prohibited; journalists must not allow payments or gifts to influence coverage or sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply ethical guiding principles rather than rigid rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Handbook is not intended as a collection of rules...journalism is a profession that has to be governed by ethical guiding principles rather than by rigid rules."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook emphasises principles and judgement over a checklist of rules. Journalists should apply ethical reasoning and professional judgement to complex situations rather than relying solely on prescriptive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act in the best interests of Reuters and its stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Handbook is "guidance to taking decisions and adopting behaviours that are in the best interests of Reuters, its shareholders, customers, contacts, readers and its profession."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-making should consider the interests of multiple stakeholders (company, shareholders, customers, contacts, readers, and the journalistic profession), balancing commercial and public-interest considerations within ethical boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in the Reuters Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Core values and standards "stem from the Reuters Trust Principles."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles are the foundational source for Reuters' editorial standards; journalists should interpret the Handbook's guidance as derived from and subordinate to those principles.
